title: Microsoft Teams: redesigned meeting controls with pin, unpin and reorder
summary: Hold: the app-pinning route omits the Edit step, and the PowerShell guidance softens Microsoft's explicit instruction not to use the cmdlet. The policy description also omits that meeting extensions follow the organiser's policy, not each attendee's policy. The rollout and default-state statements match Microsoft's supplied notice.

claims.quote: You can now customize the meeting toolbar by pinning, unpinning, and reordering controls to match how you work.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The roadmap, supplied notice and adoption page name no licence or charge specific to this redesign.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams redesigned meeting controls license meter; Teams licensing requirements each user Teams license meetings. Read roadmap, MC1317197, adoption page and Learn licensing excerpts; no redesign-specific licence or charge is named.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because entitlement to the redesigned controls is not yet published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the entitlement statements and licensing open question with: 'Microsoft documents a Teams licence as the general requirement for organisational users, except when joining meetings anonymously; no licence or charge specific to this redesign is published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access and use that wording in the notes, cost paragraph and cost rationale.

claims.claim: No meter is documented specifically for the redesigned meeting controls as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams redesigned meeting controls license meter. Read adoption page, MC1317197 and Learn excerpts on licensing, Premium and API billing; none names a meter for this toolbar redesign.

claims.claim: The editing route is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Setup policies > policy > Pinned apps > Add apps.
claims.quote: Choose the policy you want to edit and then select Edit. ... Under Pinned apps, select Add apps.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.path and the rendered path with 'Teams apps > Setup policies > policy > Edit > Pinned apps > Add apps'. Keep the surface Teams admin center and the existing docs URL.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsAppSetupPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AppPresetMeetingList <list> is presented as usable automation for meeting-app pinning, with only a recommendation to modify policies in the admin centre.
claims.quote: The existence of this cmdlet is being documented for completeness, but do not use this cmdlet. We require that all creation and modification of app setup polices
claims.fix: Keep the documented call, whose cmdlet and parameters exist, but replace the PowerShell qualifier in controls[1].note, the rendered note and the concluding paragraph with: 'Microsoft documents this cmdlet for completeness but explicitly says not to use it; all creation and modification of app setup policies, excluding assignment or removal from users, must happen in the Teams admin center.' Keep the existing reference URL.

claims.claim: A Teams Administrator or administrator with a higher role can manage app setup policies.
claims.quote: A Teams Administrator or an admin with a higher role can manage these policies.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Meeting-app pinning is described as governing users under a setup policy without qualifying which meetings follow that policy.
claims.quote: When apps are pinned for specific users, the meeting extension is available only in meetings organized by users assigned the app setup policy. In those meetings, the meeting extension is also available to other participants.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].governs and its rendered label with 'Which apps are pinned in meetings organised by users assigned a setup policy'. Add to its note: 'For policies assigned to specific users, meeting extensions are available only in meetings organised by those users and are also available to other participants.' Replace the pilot bullet with 'Confirm in meetings organised by pilot users assigned the policy that pinned apps appear in the main meeting bar or More menu as expected.'

claims.claim: The documented app-pinning control is not a control over the redesigned layout of built-in meeting buttons.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting controls redesign tenant policy PowerShell. Read MC1317197, app setup policy and Set-CsTeamsAppSetupPolicy references, and adoption page; app-pinning settings describe apps, not repositioning built-in meeting buttons.

claims.claim: App setup policy changes can take a few hours to take effect after editing or assignment.
claims.quote: After you edit or assign a policy, it can take a few hours for changes to take effect.

claims.claim: No redesign-specific Microsoft Learn setting is documented; the sources describe app setup policies as the relevant existing admin-side pinning control.
claims.quote: Searched: new meeting controls toolbar tenant disable settings Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; Teams meeting controls redesign tenant policy PowerShell. Read adoption, app setup policy and cmdlet pages and Learn policy-reference excerpts; no redesign switch was documented.
